issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Meal is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) and the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) declare Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first). The template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). The template's Main.java example (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) also constructs Meal using (name, ingredients). This mismatch will cause confusion and compilation or usage errors when students follow the example code or the UML but the template constructor has the parameters swapped.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the parameter usage inside the constructor so it assigns name to this.name and ingredients to this.ingredients. Ensure example usages (Main.java) and any other callers use the (name, ingredients) ordering to match the problem statement UML and the solution implementation.
